claims.claim: The rigidly translated original 87-face faceted core preserves its recognizable local relief.
The one-layer 60-edge/120-triangle annulus does not read as a wall or slab.
The delta introduces no visible seam or spike.
The delta introduces no depth inversion or registration loss.
Intentional negative space remains undamaged and no unintended gap closure occurs.
The evidence supports continuing this method to an application candidate.

first_concrete_failure.description: At the inner/elbow-side transition, the one-layer annulus forms a conspicuous fan of long nearly coplanar triangles. It reads as a broad sharp shelf or wall with multiple spike-like silhouette tips and crowds the source's deeper compact negative-space opening.

visual_evidence.source_current_order: source on left in gray; current on right in cyan

inspected_pairs.observation: Current gains a dominant fan of long planar triangles at the inner elbow transition. The fan creates a broad shelf or wall, several spike-like outer-silhouette projections, and visibly compresses the source's dark local opening.
The reverse view independently confirms a sharp triangular shelf projecting from the elbow/upper-forearm transition. It has no source counterpart and crowds the source's recessed gap.

The changed transition is mostly occluded, but the global arm pose, upper mass, wrist opening, long rails, and broad negative spaces remain registered; no whole-object registration loss or global depth inversion is visible.

visual_evidence.decisive_observation: The original core relief survives the rigid translation, but the one-layer annulus is visibly unacceptable: it replaces a compact recessed transition with a broad triangulated shelf or wall, creates spike-like projections in opposite views, and damages intentional negative space.

failures: The one-layer annulus creates a visible broad triangular shelf or wall.
The transition creates spike-like silhouette projections in both dorsal and ventral views.
The annulus crowds and partially bridges the source's intentional local negative space.
Exact clearance remains unresolved with 296 cutter penetrations and 704 triangle overlaps globally.
follow_up: Reject this one-layer relief-core annulus method and do not apply it to the active repair scene.
Preserve the experiment, sanitized evidence, checkpoint, and review as method-bound evidence.
Retain the useful constraint that rigid movement preserves core relief, but use a transition strategy that distributes deformation without a broad fan of long triangles or gap closure.
